questions.q: A company changes the method of measuring a class of PPE from cost to revaluation model. This is treated as:
o: Change in accounting policy — retrospective adjustment with restated comparatives
questions.why: Switching measurement model = change in POLICY ⇒ retrospective (Ind AS 8), unless a transitional provision applies. Change in depreciation method/useful life = estimate ⇒ prospective. The pairing is the trap.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: HIGH likelihood for Nov 2026 — policy/estimate/error triage is the most frequent Ind AS 8 question Prediction is study guidance, not an ICAI statement.

mem.tip: Ind AS 8 triage: policy → rewind the tape (retrospective); estimate → forward only; error → correct restated truth. Measure-model swap = policy.

questions.q: During FY26 a company revises the useful life of a machine from 10 to 6 years (asset commissioned FY21). Ind AS 8 requires:
o: Prospective depreciation over the revised remaining life
No change — life fixed at acquisition
questions.why: Revision of useful life is a change in accounting estimate: apply prospectively to current and future periods; no restatement of comparatives.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — prospective-vs-retrospective triggers dominate Ind AS 8 MCQs AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Estimate changes look forward; policy changes look back. Lives, residuals, patterns — all forward.

questions.q: An investment property is valued using observable rental yields and recent transactions of comparable buildings in the same market. Under the Ind AS 113 hierarchy this is:
o: Not fair value — use cost model
questions.why: Level 2 = observable inputs other than quoted prices in active markets (comparables, yields). Level 1 = unadjusted quoted price for the SAME asset in an active market; Level 3 = unobservable inputs.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — hierarchy-level identification is a repeat visitor AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: L1 same-and-listed; L2 observable-but-adjusted; L3 home-grown assumptions. If a broker could pull it, it isn't L3.

questions.q: Material uncertainty about an entity's ability to continue as going concern is disclosed:
o: In the financial statements, with adequate disclosure of the uncertainty; and management's intent to mitigate
questions.why: Ind AS 1 requires disclosure of material uncertainties (judgments and sources of estimation) when management identifies them; management prepares on going-concern basis unless intending to liquidate/cease trade.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — disclosure obligation vs management intent is repeatedly tested AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Uncertainty disclosed, basis still GC — unless management intends the end: then break-up basis.

questions.q: Fair value measurement assumes the transaction occurs in:
o: The principal (or most advantageous) market for the asset/liability
questions.why: Ind AS 113: fair value is an exit price in the principal (or most advantageous) market from market-participant perspective, at measurement date under orderly transaction conditions.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the principal-vs-most-advantageous rule is exact 1-marker material AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Principal market if it exists; else most advantageous. Market participants set the price, you merely witness it.

questions.q: Qualifying asset for capitalising borrowing costs is one that:
o: Necessarily takes a substantial period of time to get ready for its intended use or sale
Is financed wholly with own funds
questions.why: Ind AS 23: qualifying asset = necessarily takes substantially more than 12 months to prepare for intended use/sale (inventories, PPE, intangibles, investment property).
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — the >12-month benchmark is the quick test Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: If 12 months or more of getting-ready, the interest belongs to the asset, not the year.

questions.q: Prudence in the 2018 Conceptual Framework means:
o: Caution under conditions of uncertainty — neutrality preserved, no excessive reserves
questions.why: Prudence = caution when estimating under uncertainty (no understating income/assets or overstating liabilities) — not a licence for systematic understatement.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — prudence-vs-reserve-busting is a signature distinction AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Prudence is careful weighing, not thumb-pressing on one side of the scale.

questions.topic: Framework VIU vs Ind AS 36 VIU
questions.q: Value in use under the Conceptual Framework differs from the impairment-standard VIU mainly because the Framework notion:
o: Is an entry-value idea — entity-specific discounted cash flows from continued use and disposal, not the regulated Ind AS 36 recipe
questions.why: The Framework describes the measurement BASE (value in use as an entry price of future flows); Ind AS 36 turns one slice of it into a prescribed recipe (pre-tax flows and discount rate inside a recoverable-amount comparison).
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — same words, different rooms — base versus recipe Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.ti: TI: Framework VIU vs Ind AS 36 VIU
mem.tip: Framework defines the concept; the standard runs one regulated experiment in it.
mem.link: Chapter 4 — Ind AS on Measurement based on Accounting Policies

questions.q: Own-credit risk in fair valuing a liability is:
o: Included (DOL — change attributable to own credit in OCI for FV-optioned liabilities)
questions.why: Ind AS 113: fair value of a liability reflects non-performance risk including own credit; for liabilities at FVTPL by election, own-credit portion to OCI (no recycle).
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the own-credit OCI lane AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Your own creditiness makes your liability cheaper to value — the discount goes to OCI, not profit.

questions.q: The 2023 amendment set to Ind AS 8 clarified how a change in a measurement TECHNIQUE is treated. A change from one estimation technique to another (not caused by a policy change) is:
o: A change in accounting estimate — prospective
questions.why: DEFINITE documented change: the 'Definition of Accounting Estimates' amendments (MCA notification; ICAI adoption effective for annual periods beginning on/after 1 April 2023) make clear that a change in measurement technique is a change in ESTIMATE unless it results from applying a new policy; the error distinction is preserved.
questions.trend: Traceable to a real, publicly-notified amendment/standard (documented fact), tested in ICAI style.
questions.probWhy: HIGH likelihood for Nov 2026 — the amendment renamed the border between technique and policy — borders get tested Prediction is study guidance, not an ICAI statement.

mem.ti: TI: Amendment — Definition of Accounting Estimates
mem.tip: Technique change = estimate (forward); only the policy itself rewinds the tape.
mem.link: Chapter 4 — Ind AS on Measurement based on Accounting Policies
